schema_description: Living Hearing Profile — sovereign, user-owned, versioned hearing data. Extends openhear-audiogram-v1 with preference, context, haptic and history layers.
subject: Lewis Burgess

clinical_core.comment: Immutable clinical measurements. Append only via history layer; never mutate in place.
clinical_core.source: Dorothy Thomson Hearing Services, 12 Southend Ave, Darlington, DL3 7HL
clinical_core.notes: Most recent verified clinical audiogram. ISQ (no significant change) from prior tests dating back to 2017-01-19. High-frequency sloping sensorineural loss — the public reference profile for OpenHear.

preference_layer.comment: User-defined loudness and comfort preferences. Evolves over time. Refined with lived-experience signals through 2026-08-25.

loudness_growth.comment: Per-frequency gain offset applied on top of clinical prescription. Positive = louder, negative = quieter. Mid-frequency lift prioritised for speech intelligibility under high-frequency sloping loss.

preference_layer.notes: Mid-band lift for speech clarity under sloping loss. Sustained listening effort leads to switching-off. Loudness intolerance / recruitment: amplified sound can become the problem — people remove aids or change programmes even when residual environmental awareness remains. Lived-experience signal (2026-08-25): deliberate aid-out recovery time (first thing in the morning and before sleep) is a common self-management strategy; the profile and any haptic path must respect intentional quiet periods rather than treating aid-out as non-compliance. One RNID panel member reported that unmatched amplification and dual-earpiece content triggered their tinnitus. This is recorded as an individual preference, not general advice: Tinnitus UK advises that amplification matched to a person's hearing can help tinnitus. Media contexts allow mono / single-sided routing where the person chooses it. When an Auracast clean feed is active, preference offsets still apply; aggressive room-noise strategies should step down.

history.comment: Append-only change log with SHA-256 content commitments (Burgess Principle compatible). Versions 2–4 were not recorded; the log is append-only from version 5.
